angle: the object in the machine's name, drawn literally and well
subject: Rain itself: the last bar's drops falling through still air, each drawn as a real drop (round on top, flattened underneath the bigger it is) with a strobe ghost where it was a moment ago, where a drop's size is its note and the one that just played is bright.
controls: rate: how many drops are in the air (count, about 7 at 1.0 a beat up to about 28 at 8, each one a note of the last bar).

roof: the spread of drop sizes (shape/scale per drop): at 0 st every drop is the same size, one note; at 36 st they range from a pin-head to a big flattened drop, so the size range is the pitch range.
gust: the fall slants (each drop and its ghost offset sideways along the wind, ±35°), and the drops sort themselves big-to-small along the gust's direction, so a run reads as a graded slope of sizes.
puddle: drops that are replays appear as hatched copies of earlier drops (45° hairlines inside a hairline outline, there but not new), from none at 0 to most of the air at 100.
reference: library/theseus-tower (an object drawn as itself, detail inside a calm outline, one lit part)
risks: Free-floating circles can read as bubbles or bells if the strobe ghosts are lost; the ghost is what says 'falling', so it can't be dropped for budget.
Each drop is ~4 nodes (outline, ghost, equator, crescent); 28 drops at rate 8 is over 100 nodes and many redraws per beat: will need a pool and a cap.
Size is both pitch and (slightly) depth: the camera puts drops nearly in one plane so perspective can't fake a pitch; keep depth range small.
Nothing roof-like remains: the 'roof' label maps to size spread, which must be learned from turning it.
Muted: drops freeze mid-air and their outlines drop to G3 hairline; no ghosts.
